$comment: Maps every section of the PRE-REFACTOR instruction surface — root CLAUDE.md plus the nine
docs/claude/ topic documents, at the git rev under 'baseline' — to where its content now
lives. This file is the evidence for the claim that the refactor RELOCATED guidance rather
It exists because the change is not reviewable from the diff. Content moved between files, so
every relocated line shows up as both a deletion and an addition; nothing in `git diff` states
that 08-metadata-and-sync.md's four sections all landed in one rule, or that two sections were
dropped on purpose. This file states it, and check-claude-md.mjs verifies the statement.
root                 -> stayed in root CLAUDE.md (unrecoverable-if-violated, or always true)
rule:<path>          -> a path-scoped rule under .claude/rules/ (loads on matching file)
skill:<name>         -> a skill under .claude/skills/ (loads on invocation)
doc:<path>           -> ordinary documentation (read on request, never auto-loaded)

note: 512 of these 645 lines were never loaded unless an agent chose to read them. Eight of the
nine topic documents were still byte-identical to the mj-sample-open-app template they were
scaffolded from, so they had also stopped tracking their upstream.
Claude Code's own guidance is ~200 lines per CLAUDE.md: longer files consume context AND
reduce adherence. The ceiling is set slightly above the achieved result so small additions
The root file did NOT get smaller (133 -> 173 lines), and that is the intended outcome, not a
regression. What changed is WHAT is resident. Four `generated/`-only footguns (old rules
7-10) left the always-loaded budget for the 385 files they actually protect, and the space
went to a routing table and a skills index — navigation, which is useful on every task, in
place of detail that was useful on almost none.
Raising this ceiling requires justifying why the new content is unrecoverable-if-violated or
true-on-every-task. If it is neither, it belongs in a rule.

sections.title: Repository structure
sections.note: Always true, and cheap. `plans/` added to the listing; `docs/claude/` dropped from it since it is now a signpost rather than a location.

sections.title: 📖 The MemberJunction development guide → docs/claude/
sections.note: The nine-row topic table became the routing table over .claude/rules/. docs/claude/README.md survives as a human-facing redirect explaining where each topic went and why.

sections.title: Rule 1 — No commits without explicit approval
sections.note: Unrecoverable: an unwanted commit rewrites shared history. Must survive /compact.

sections.title: Rule 2 — Never edit src/generated/
sections.note: Path-scoped to the files it protects, where it now loads on open instead of being recited on every task.

sections.title: Rule 3 — Never edit an applied migration
Rule 4 — Branch rules
sections.note: Split: the tracking half stays in root because wrong tracking pushes straight to next and bypasses review. The 'migration PR needs a changeset >= minor' half moved to the rule that loads when you open .changeset/.

sections.title: Rule 5 — Single-copy invariant
sections.note: Unrecoverable and true on every task in linked mode: a stray npm install duplicates packages and fails far from the cause.

sections.title: Rule 6 — When linked into MJ, wiring edits are local-only
sections.note: Unrecoverable in another repo's history — the worst place to discover a mistake.

sections.title: Rule 7 — mj sync push runs from the MJ repo cwd
sections.note: Including all three sub-bullets: --no-app-packages, the 16GB heap ceiling, and the geocoding split between People/Organizations and Addresses.

sections.title: Rule 10 — Never tidy RecurrenceMonths: null away
sections.note: The four GUIDs, the PushService.ts:1163 mechanism, and the calendar-month-applicability explanation all retained verbatim — this one is only correct in full.

sections.title: Build & dev commands
sections.note: check:claude-md added to the gate list.

sections.title: No `any` types — ever
sections.note: With both corollaries: no .Get()/.Set() where a typed property exists, and derive value-list unions from the entity instead of hand-copying.

sections.title: No destructive git operations without explicit approval
sections.note: Promoted INTO root. It was previously only in a file nothing loaded — the single most consequential rule in the set with the weakest delivery.

sections.title: No dynamic import() unless narrowly justified
Persist user preferences via UserInfoEngine — never localStorage
Always run and update unit tests
sections.note: Retargeted. The obligation is kept, but pointed at the gate suite rather than at `npm test`, which passes vacuously here — all three packages ship echo stubs. repo-gates.md says so explicitly so the green light is not mistaken for evidence.

sections.title: App-repo additions (this template's own rules)
sections.note: Duplicated the root rules 2 and 3 it sat alongside; both now have exactly one home.

sections.title: Feature branches MUST track same-named remote branches
Creating entity objects — always via Metadata
entity_object vs simple (the biggest easy win)
sections.note: 03 and 04 merged into one rule. They share a glob (**/*.ts) and are read together — splitting them would have produced two shallow files loading in lockstep.

sections.title: Batch everything
sections.note: Merged with 03's RunViews bullet, which said the same thing — an accidental duplication the split had hidden.

sections.title: What CodeGen generates (never write these by hand)
The change workflow (order matters)
sections.note: Intentionally in both: migrations.md states the ordering for someone writing a migration, generated-code.md states the commit-together obligation for someone looking at generated output. Each states only its own half.

sections.title: Record Changes (built-in versioning)
sections.note: Moved to the data rule: it is a don't-build-your-own-audit-trail instruction for someone writing TypeScript, not migration guidance.

sections.title: Design tokens — no hardcoded colors
sections.note: Kept, but deliberately NOT given its own **/*.scss rule the way MJ has one. This repo has zero SCSS; its three .css files are a static marketing site under website/assets/ with no MJ token system. angular.md is scoped to packages/Angular/** and says so, so the rule cannot fire on the website.

sections.title: Functional decomposition is mandatory
sections.note: Softened from a line-count rule to a smell-to-investigate: decompose by abstraction, not by length. A cohesive deep function beats several shallow helpers that must be read together.

sections.title: Commands
sections.note: Merged with root rule 7, which restated the same push discipline in different words. The two had already drifted — root carried the heap ceiling, this one carried the parallel-batch-size and AfterCreate detail, and neither carried both.

sections.title: The framework
sections.note: Reduced to the one durable sentence — Vitest is MJ's standard, Jest is deprecated — recorded as what to adopt IF a real suite is added.

sections.title: Running
sections.note: Commands replaced. `npm run test:watch` and `npx turbo run test --filter=...[HEAD~1]` address a suite that does not exist here; the gate commands that do run took their place.

sections.title: Writing
sections.reason: Describes a Vitest suite this repo does not have: src/__tests__/<Source>.test.ts layout, vi mocking, @memberjunction/test-utils helpers, and a describe/it skeleton. There are ZERO *.test.ts files here and all three packages ship `"test": "echo 'No tests configured yet'"`. repo-gates.md documents the conventions for the tests this repo DOES have — node --test, scripts/*.spec.mjs, throwaway temp-dir repo roots. Keeping both would have shipped two contradictory testing conventions, and the one describing nothing would have been indistinguishable from the one describing the gates.

sections.title: Expectations
sections.note: Report pass/fail/skip honestly, and say what was not run. Kept, with the vacuous-npm-test warning attached so the honesty requirement has teeth here.

newContent.$comment: Not part of the baseline — authored with this change. Listed so the gate's routing check has a complete picture and so a reader can tell relocated content from new.

entries.why: The gate conventions — every gate carries its own test, skips must be visible, the header comment carries the incident — were enforced by CI and described in changes.yml comments, but stated in no instruction file. An agent adding a gate had to infer them from the neighbours.
The fixed group means one minor bumps all three packages. That was implicit in .changeset/config.json and nowhere in prose.
The rationale for this arrangement, so the next person to add guidance knows where it goes and why the root file is not the default answer.
The gate. Without it the budget is an intention rather than a property of the repo.
